# SSH-004: Empty passwords are refused

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** critical
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

PermitEmptyPasswords yes lets an account whose password is empty log in with no secret at all.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -i '^permitemptypasswords'
```

## How to fix it

Set PermitEmptyPasswords no (the default) and lock accounts with empty passwords (passwd -l).

Run `stackward explain SSH-004` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
